zh: 戴顿大学是一所位于美国俄亥俄州戴顿的天主教私立大学. 全日制大学生有7,500人，全体学生是11,000人，提供70种学术课程. 戴顿大学是全美国第一所提供人权学士学位的大学.

戴顿大学的前身为“圣玛丽男子学校”（英文：St. Mary's School for Boys）简称“圣玛丽学院”（英文：St. Mary's Institute）. 1849年，天主教圣母司铎会（Society of Mary (Marists)）牧师利欧·梅耶 （Rev. Leo Meyer, S.M.）从法国阿尔萨斯来到美国俄亥俄州辛辛那提传教. 时逢俄亥俄州霍乱横行，辛辛那提教区主教约翰·巴蒂斯特·珀塞尔（John Baptist Purcell）将其分配至位于戴顿市的以马内利堂区传教. 在当地，梅耶牧师结识了来自欧洲的移民约翰·斯图尔特（John Stuart）. 斯图尔特的女儿玛丽·露易莎·斯图尔特与一年前因霍乱去世. 万念俱灰之下，斯图尔特和妻子希望将其拥有的农场售予教会并返回欧洲.

次年（1850年）3月19日，梅耶牧师和其他三名圣母司铎会会员：教师马克西姆·泽勒（Maximin Zehler），厨师查尔斯·舒尔茨（Charles Schultz）以及园丁安德鲁·埃德尔（Andrew Edel）合计，买下斯图尔特的农场，并以耶稣基督故乡——拿撒勒（Nazareth）命名. 农场占地125英亩，含有果园，一座住房，各种附属农业设施. 未来的学校将在此建立. 约翰·斯图尔特夭折的女儿玛丽的坟墓被保留并得到妥善维护. 1850年7月1日，圣玛丽男子学校（St. Mary's School for Boys）正式开学.

之后数年，学校迅速发展. 虽然与1855年遭遇火灾，校舍被焚毁，但学校迅速得以重建并继续扩张. 至1860年泽勒出任校长时，学生规模超过100人. 美国内战对学校影响甚微，盖因其学生年幼，无法充任军职之故. 次年，圣玛丽学院开始提供大学预科和预备修士课程，并于1882年起成为具有完整的学士学位授予权的高等院校，获得俄亥俄州的承认，学校名称也与1878年微调为St. Mary's College. 此时的圣玛丽学院仍提供高中教育.
1920年，为增强与所在城市的联系并增强其普适性，圣玛丽学院改名为“戴顿大学”（英文：University of Dayton）. 同时高中部亦独立，发展成如今的夏明纳-茱莉安纳高级中学（Chaminade Julienne High School）.
en: The University of Dayton (UD) is a private, Catholic research university in Dayton, Ohio, United States. Founded in 1850 by the Society of Mary, it is one of three Marianist universities in the US and the second-largest private university in Ohio. Its campus is located in southern Dayton and spans 388 acres on both sides of the Great Miami River. The campus is noted for the Immaculate Conception Chapel and the University of Dayton Arena.

As of 2023, the university enrolls approximately 11,300 undergraduate and postgraduate students from a variety of religious, ethnic and geographic backgrounds. It offers more than 80 academic programs in the arts, sciences, business, education, health sciences, engineering, and law. In 2009, UD offered what it believes to be one of the first undergraduate degree programs in human rights. It is classified among "R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity".

In 1849, on a mission to establish a presence for the Society of Mary in America, Leo Meyer journeyed from Alsace in France to Cincinnati. But with a cholera epidemic raging to the north, Bishop John Baptist Purcell of the Cincinnati diocese sent Meyer to Emmanuel parish in Dayton to tend to the sick. In Dayton, Meyer met local farmer John Stuart, who had lost his infant daughter Mary Louisa to cholera the year before. Heartbroken, Stuart and his wife wanted to sell their Dewberry Farm property and return to Europe.

On March 19, 1850, Meyer, joined by three Marianist brothers—teacher Maximin Zehler, cook Charles Schultz, and gardener Andrew Edel—purchased the 125 acre hilltop farm from Stuart and renamed it Nazareth. Stuart accepted a St. Joseph medal and a promise of $12,000 at 6 percent interest. The property included vineyards, an orchard, a mansion, various farm buildings, and the grave of Stuart's daughter, which Meyer promised to maintain.

Just a few months later, the University of Dayton had its beginning on July 1, 1850, when St. Mary's School for Boys opened its doors to 14 primary students from Dayton. In September the first boarding students arrived and classes moved to the mansion. Five years later, the school burned to the ground, but classes resumed within months. By 1860, when Zehler became president, the enrollment was nearly 100 students. The Civil War had little direct effect on the school because most of the students were too young to serve. College preparatory classes started in 1861 along with a novitiate and school for Marianist candidates. The school became Chaminade High School, named after the order's founder William Joseph Chaminade, which has since merged with the all-girls Julienne High school run by the Sisters of Notre Dame de Namur to form the coeducational Chaminade-Julienne High School.
